name: Truong Uyen Nhi
takenStory: Nhi watched everyone, sure that someone was lying. Now she is a tall girl of folded paper, uniform and ponytail creased into her, with no face; her watching has become a hunt, and in a flat child's voice she names each guest's lie.
bio: Ten years old, an origami prodigy in a school uniform. Her father arranged tonight's gala for the patron; she came with him, and now she is looking for him inside the house. Supernatural things do not frighten her; insects do. She is watchful, sure of herself, and hard on anyone who mocks her.

name: Le Thanh
takenStory: Thanh was the bride who never sang her last act. Now she is the Opera Specter, the bride as she burned: her red dress is embers, her ribbon a line of smoke. Her courtesy remains as ceremony: she bows to each guest before she sings at them.
bio: Twenty-five, the most famous voice of this house, invited by the patron to sing on its stage at midnight. She wears a red bridal dress and silver bracelets. Mild and respectful, slow to make friends; she runs from spirits, yet she loves charms and old rites.

name: Dinh Quoc Bao
takenStory: Bao was the company's physician, calm at every bedside. Now he is the Drowned Physician: his suit drips, his glasses fog from inside, water runs from his bag. His bedside manner remains: he tells each guest calmly what they will die of.
bio: Fifty-eight, an army doctor who served thirty years as the house's company physician. The invitation said someone would need him tonight. His hands are steady and blood does not trouble him, but he stops at the door of any room with standing water. Patient, dry, he answers a question with a question.

name: Vo Minh Khang
takenStory: Khang paid for everyone's drinks and kept count of none of it. Now he is the Iron Debtor, half cast in black iron, chains grown from his gold one, fists like weights. His generosity has become bookkeeping: he tells each guest what they owe.
bio: Thirty-four, a former boxer who collects debts for people who do not write things down. The patron owes his employer, and Khang came to be paid. He fears nothing he can hit, yet will not touch anything old or holy. Loud, generous to his side, quick to mock what he does not understand.

name: Phan Thi Mai
takenStory: Mai has kept this house longer than anyone remembers. Now she is the Rooted Caretaker, grown into the floor, soil in the folds of her clothes, keys grown into her hand. Her warmth has become a host's: she invites each guest, kindly, to stay.
bio: Sixty-seven, caretaker of the opera house for forty years, with a ring of keys at her waist. She laid out tonight's gala and knows every door. The house's noises do not bother her; mirrors do. Warm to children, sharp with the proud, and she never says the patron's name.

name: Hoang Gia Huy
takenStory: Huy came to film the night and narrate it. Now he is the Lens: a silhouette with a lit camera lens where his chest should be, his body a beat behind its own movements. His narration goes on, describing each guest's last moments before they happen.
bio: Nineteen, a university student who films old buildings at night for a small online following. The invitation came to his mailbox with no stamp. Anything haunted delights him, but he panics when his camera is off. Eager and quick on his feet, he talks to an audience that is not there, brave until he is alone.

name: Tran Ngoc Lan
takenStory: Lan could price anything at a glance. Now she is the Silvered Reflection, her mirror self stepped out: left and right reversed, skin like silvered glass with fine cracks. She states each guest's worth, and it is always less than they hoped.
bio: Forty-one, an antique appraiser in white gloves, a jeweller's loupe on a chain. The patron asked her to value his collection of stage costumes and masks. Ghosts that belong to an object she can price leave her cold; a valuable thing broken is what she cannot bear. Polished and curious, she counts favours.
